source_read: PDF (version of record), pp. 60-72, all 13 pages: text extracted with pdftotext -layout and read in full; pp. 63, 68, 69 and 70 checked on pages rendered at 150 dpi; Tables 1-4 (printed sideways, pp. 64-67) rotated and read at 170-220 dpi. Nine-study ranges, medians and means recomputed from Table 4; reviewer-calculated estimates ('a') counted in Tables 1-3. The online Supplementary Material was not among the files and was not read.

claims.overstatement: Two wording points are not accurate as worded. (1) 'a review of 124 published estimates': by my count of the 'a' (own calculation) marks in Tables 1-3, 71 of the 124 (31 of 37 method-1, 14 of 36 method-2 and 26 of 51 method-3 estimates) were calculated by the reviewers from the studies' data rather than published by the studies (pp. 63-66). They include the 2.7% minimum of the overall range (Timko et al., 1995, method 1), all of the nine-study method-1 range except Dawson et al. (2005)'s four values, and the 14.0% at 16 years. Suggested wording: '124 estimates, over half of them calculated by the reviewers from the studies' data'. 'These figures are second-hand' should allow for that. (2) In the magnitude, '36.0% vs 14.0% (remission once vs also at 16 years)': the 36.0% already required remission at both the 1-year and 3-year follow-ups (Table 2, p. 65), so it should read 'at 1 and 3 years vs also at 16 years'. The statement's own wording ('when recovery also had to hold 16 years later') is correct.
claims.note: All numbers from Mellor in the statement and magnitude were found on the rendered pages: 124 estimates, 27 studies, 1976-2018, 24 (89%) North American, 2.7%-98.3% (p. 63); 78% untreated among the remitted in two Canadian surveys (p. 63; Table 3, p. 66: 77.7% Ontario and 77.5% national, with remission meaning abstinence or moderate drinking; with abstinence only 56.0% and 65.7%); NESARC 2001-02 12.4% and 32.6% (p. 69; Table 2, p. 65); Netherlands 78% and 40% (p. 69; Table 2 prints 77.9% and 40.6%); Moos and Moos (2007) 36.0% and 14.0% (Table 2; p. 69); nine studies: method 1 2.7%-63.6%, method 2 6.5%-77.9%, method 3 4.3%-94.2%, medians 12.4, 38.9 and 43.9 (pp. 63, 68), all reproduced from Table 4 (p. 67). Qualifications: (a) the method-3 low end of 4.3% comes from Table 4's entries for Timko et al. (2000), which repeat that study's method-1 values; Table 3 gives 8.0%-27.6%, and with those values the nine-study method-3 range is 6.4%-94.2% (median 43.9, mean 44.0; my calculation). (b) 'Most estimates covered about one year': the paper says a majority of studies used a one-year window (p. 69) or 6-12 months (p. 70), not a majority of estimates. (c) 'People initially without treatment' in the Moos and Moos cohort means people seen once for detox or at an information and referral centre without other treatment (Table 2 note b). (d) 'The review did not appraise the studies' is supported (p. 70). The review states it was not designed to give rates (p. 61), and its abstract opens by calling untreated remission common (p. 60) without quantifying that. The claim's synthesis sentence (a high share never treated among the remitted, and a much lower share of everyone with a problem remitting untreated in a year) matches the review's ordering of the three methods (p. 69).

anchors.extracted: Systematic searches (Medline, PsycINFO, EMBASE and other sources; 2,103 texts) for peer-reviewed articles since 1975 giving numeric estimates of untreated remission from alcohol problems; narrative synthesis; 124 estimates from 27 studies; three sampling methods (all people with alcohol problems, untreated people, people already remitted). The background calls untreated remission common without a figure.

27 studies published 1976-2018; 24 (89%) in North America; 12 longitudinal; 20 (74%) convenience samples, 1 probability sample, population-based data from the US, Canada, Germany and the Netherlands. The 124 estimates ranged from 2.7% to 98.3%, a spread attributed to the starting sample and to definitions of problem, remission and treatment.

Method 1 (share of all people with an alcohol problem who remit without treatment): 37 estimates from 11 studies, only two of which (Bischof et al., 2005; Dawson et al., 2005) estimated it directly; the rest were calculated by the reviewers (31 of 37 marked as own calculation in Table 1, including the 2.7% for Timko et al., 1995).

Method 2 (share of untreated people who remit): 36 estimates from 16 studies; studies of one cohort of untreated people found 14.0%-52.9%. Method 3 (share of remitted people never treated): 51 estimates from 19 studies, the commonest approach; Sobell et al. (1996), two Canadian population surveys: 78% of people with a lifetime drinking problem but none in the past year had not been treated (Table 3: 77.7% and 77.5% with abstinence or moderate drinking; 56.0% and 65.7% with abstinence only).

Nine studies with all three methods, 23 estimates each: method 1 2.7%-63.6% (median 12.4, mean 21.5); method 2 6.5%-77.9% (median 38.9, mean 40.9); method 3 4.3%-94.2% (median 43.9, mean 42.7). Same numerators, larger denominator for method 1. Recomputed from Table 4: identical.

anchors.locator: Table 4, Timko et al. (2000) rows, against Table 3 (p. 66)
anchors.extracted: Table 4 gives Timko et al. (2000)'s method-3 values as 4.3, 11.2, 7.3 and 16.1, the same as its method-1 values; Table 3 gives 8.0, 20.9, 12.5 and 27.6. With Table 3's values the nine-study method-3 range is 6.4%-94.2%, median 43.9, mean 44.0 (my calculation).

anchors.locator: Results > 3.2.2 Definition of remission, 1st paragraph; Table 2 (p. 65)
anchors.extracted: NESARC 2001-02 (Dawson et al., 2005), untreated people with lifetime alcohol dependence (method 2): 12.4% remitted when remission meant abstinence in the past year, 32.6% when abstinence or moderate drinking; Table 2 adds 46.5% (also no consequences) and 76.2% (also no diagnosis).

anchors.locator: Results > 3.2.1 Definition of an alcohol problem, 3rd paragraph; Table 2 (p. 65)
anchors.extracted: Tuithof et al. (2016), Netherlands: of people with an alcohol use disorder who stayed untreated across the 3-year study, 78% (Table 2: 77.9%) had no diagnosis in the past year at the 3-year follow-up; among those with a moderate or severe disorder, 40% (Table 2: 40.6%).

anchors.locator: Table 2, Moos and Moos (2007) rows and note b; Results > 3.2.2, 2nd paragraph (p. 69)
anchors.extracted: Untreated people from the Timko et al. (1993) cohort (seen once for detox or at an information and referral centre, without other treatment): 36.0% in remission at both the 1-year and 3-year follow-ups; 14.0% (reviewers' calculation) when remission also had to hold at 16 years.

For the majority of studies remission meant one year without alcohol problems (6-12 months, p. 70), and most asked about remission at one point in time; the authors say the estimates suit planning over one year.

No assessment of methodological quality or bias was made, and only journal articles were included; the review states it was not meant to yield rates for direct use but to examine methods and definitions.

key_findings.correction: Worth adding: Sobell's 78% is the abstinence-or-moderate-drinking figure (77.7% and 77.5%); with abstinence only, 56.0% and 65.7% (Table 3, p. 66).
Worth adding: the 14.0% is marked as the reviewers' own calculation (Table 2), and the 36.0% required remission at both the 1-year and 3-year follow-ups.
Small wording point: the paper says a majority of studies (not estimates) used 6-12-month windows (p. 70).

reporting_issues.note: Found independently in my blind reading; recomputed 6.4% minimum, mean 44.0, median 43.9.
My count of 'a' marks: 31 of 37 (method 1), 14 of 36 (method 2), 26 of 51 (method 3), 71 of 124 in all.

risk_of_bias.note: Editors' narrative-review checklist, overall high from the appraisal domain (no quality or bias assessment, p. 70). The card's calculations recompute: Table 1 median 14.8 with 28 of 37 below 30%; 24 of 27 studies before 2010.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor; the abstract's unquantified premise and the method-1 robustness statement against Table 1 are both on the cited pages.

missed: Provenance of the estimates: 71 of the 124 (57%) are the reviewers' own calculations, including the 2.7% minimum of the overall range. can_establish ('published estimates ... span 2.7% to 98.3%') and the design_detail should say so (Tables 1-3, pp. 64-66).
